quote: when a state has spent fifteen years iterating
correct_fact: Blueprint dates from 2006 and PCMHs from 2008; Ch8 calls it a twenty-year record / nearly two decades.
source_quote: Since 2008, Vermont has adopted and evolved with this model of care

quote: the comprehensive primary health care vision embedded in Act 68
correct_fact: Act 68 does not enumerate the five-component vision (see ch08 finding on line 3906); align wording.
source_quote: § 9403b Steering Committee duties

quote: For practices that have not previously sought NCQA recognition --- and many of Vermont's smaller rural practices have not --- the transformation process is operationally intensive and typically requires 12-18 months of preparation.
correct_fact: Blueprint: 124 practices recognized/sustained in 2025 and MHI covers 93% of PCMHs; no source that 'many' rural practices lack recognition or for 12-18 months. Blueprint does say renewing practices begin preparing six to nine months ahead.
source_quote: Typically, these practices began active preparation work six to nine months ahead of their anniversary date

quote: The 2023 PCMH Standards represent the current requirements:
correct_fact: Six concept areas confirmed (TC, KM, AC, CM, CC, QI). Blueprint 2025 report: practices are preparing to meet new standard requirements for 2026.
source_quote: Practices are currently preparing to meet new standard requirements for 2026.

quote: Vermont's 76% rate (HEDIS FUM)
correct_fact: AHS: 30-Day Follow-Up After ED Visit for Mental Illness 76% (summary table; appendix shows 81%), PCMH-attributed, 2023.
source_quote: 30-Day Follow-Up After ED Visit for Mental Illness 76%

quote: Each of Vermont's 13 Hospital Service Areas has at least one Blueprint field staff member --- typically a Quality Improvement Facilitator
correct_fact: 13 QI Facilitators each assigned to a geographic area, plus locally hired Program Managers and CHT Leaders.
source_quote: Presently, there are thirteen QI Facilitators (13 FTE) assigned to work with Blueprint-participating practices in a geographic area.

quote: which ended with the All-Payer Model in 2025 and which state funds are offsetting in 2026 after Vermont withdrew from AHEAD --- is the most operationally significant clinical program transition
correct_fact: The CY2026 state backfill was appropriated in the FY2026 budget (Feb 2025) because AHEAD Medicare payments were not expected until 2028 — before, not after, the July 2026 withdrawal. 'Most operationally significant' is an unsourced superlative.
source_quote: payments are currently expected to begin in 2028. Because of this gap between federal models, the legislature appropriated funding for Blueprint PCMHs and CHTs to cover more than $5 million in Medicare payments for CY2026.

quote: can manage a panel of 1,500-2,000 patients --- significantly larger than the 1,100-1,200 typically associated with solo or minimally supported practice ... expand effective panel capacity by 30-50%
correct_fact: Closest source: Altschuler et al., Ann Fam Med 2012;10(5):396-400 — with delegation scenarios, reasonable panels of 1,387, 1,523 or 1,947. No source found for the 1,100-1,200 baseline or the 30-50% figure.
source_quote: panel sizes of 1,947, 1,523, or 1,387 patients

quote: The 3-5% of complex patients in Tier 1 typically account for 30-40% of total cost of care for the panel.
correct_fact: Nationally the costliest 5% account for about half of spending (MEPS: 48.8% in 2019; >50% in 2021); top 1% ~22-24%. 30-40% understates. Same figure in Fig 9.5 attributed to 'Blueprint' (no Blueprint source).
source_quote: the top 5 percent ... accounted for ... more than half of total health care expenditures (MEPS Statistical Brief #556, 2021 data)

quote: prevents one hospitalization per month ... generates approximately $180,000 in avoided cost annually
correct_fact: Implies ~$15,000 per admission, an unstated assumption; make it explicit.

quote: Panel risk stratification is a core requirement of PCMH recognition under any major accrediting body (NCQA, URAC, or state-specific equivalents)
correct_fact: No source that every accreditor makes stratification a core requirement; NCQA treats care-management identification as a criterion. Soften.

quote: The telepsychiatry model is Vermont's primary solution. Several Vermont-based telepsychiatry services, including consultation-liaison programs through UVMMC and regional mental health providers, can provide
correct_fact: No source found for named Vermont telepsychiatry CoCM services; the only RHT-funded item is a real-time psychiatric consultation program for pediatric and perinatal providers (activity #10).
source_quote: build capacity for pediatric and perinatal providers through a program that provides real-time psychiatric consultation, training, and resources

quote: One psychiatrist ... can support 10-15 primary care practices
correct_fact: Consistent with AIMS Center time estimates (~60 min caseload review per BHCM weekly plus prep/documentation, i.e. ~2-3 h per BHCM); no explicit 10-15 figure published. Low risk; kept.
source_quote: 60 minutes per BHCM for the Systematic Caseload Review (for a typical size caseload)

quote: Vermont's RHT Program application identifies BHCM workforce training as a specific investment priority.
correct_fact: No BHCM line in the RHT application/activity list. RHT funds Blueprint transformation-network capacity incl. MH/SUD integration (#16) and CHT workforce support/training (#17).
source_quote: 16 Enhancing Blueprint transformation network capacity ... Priority areas include ... integration of MH/SUD and physical health

quote: The 80% of Blueprint administrative entities that reported increased CHT staffing in the 2025 MHI evaluation
correct_fact: 80% unsourced; Blueprint: 62.2 FTE MHI-funded, all HSAs hired. (Fig 9.3 row with the same 80% claim is covered by the count-2 pair in ch08_pairs.json.)
source_quote: 62.2 FTE staff positions are currently providing care thanks to the MHI funding ... All HSAs have hired staff

quote: Given Vermont's population of approximately 60,000-70,000 adults with type 2 diabetes ... implies on the order of 13,000-15,400 patients
correct_fact: AHS/VDH BRFSS 2023: 9% of Vermont adults ever diagnosed with diabetes; ~528,000 adults (82% of 644,663) -> ~45,000-50,000; x22% -> ~10,000-11,000.
source_quote: Vermont Adults Who Have Ever Been Diagnosed with Diabetes 9% 13%

quote: 68% after SUD ED visits
correct_fact: Alcohol-use measure. Covered by the count-2 pair '68% after SUD ED visits.' in ch08_pairs.json — do not apply twice.
source_quote: 30-Day Follow-Up After ED Visit for Alcohol Use 68%

quote: The 2025 AHS transformation report notes below-benchmark cervical cancer screening rates in several Vermont communities
correct_fact: Neither the Nov 2025 nor June 2026 AHS outcome-measure report contains any cervical cancer screening measure.
source_quote: (no occurrence of 'cervical' in the report)

quote: which determines the organization's global budget ... translates directly into a lower global budget ... (Key Concepts) directly affecting global budget levels
correct_fact: Act 68 global-budget methodology is still under GMCB design; 'population adjustment' for complexity is an open design question. RAF drives risk-adjusted payments/benchmarks (MA, ACOs), not, as of now, Vermont hospital global budgets.
source_quote: Population adjustment: How budgets account for patient demographics, complexity, and socioeconomic factors ... Key tradeoffs: ... administrative simplicity vs. sophisticated risk adjustment

quote: The three most common HCC documentation opportunities in Vermont's primary care population ... diabetes complications (Vermont's primary care population has high rates of diabetic nephropathy, neuropathy, and retinopathy
correct_fact: No Vermont source for 'most common' or 'high rates'. Under CMS-HCC V28 (fully phased in for 2026) diabetes HCCs 36-38 are constrained to one coefficient, so documenting complications no longer raises the diabetes HCC weight (CKD stage 3+ and morbid obesity still carry their own HCCs).
source_quote: V28 constrained HCC 36, HCC 37, and HCC 38 to the same 0.166 community coefficient

quote: Vermont's Community Health Teams have developed a care transition protocol that represents current best practice ... Blueprint practices that have implemented this protocol systematically report 30-day readmission rates below the Vermont statewide average.
correct_fact: No Blueprint document found describing this protocol or reporting such readmission results; present it as a model protocol and drop the results claim.

quote: One of the clearest findings from Oliver Wyman's Act 167 community engagement process was that Vermont's clinical leaders ... were not systematically engaged ... the clinical leaders often were not.
correct_fact: Oliver Wyman reports no such finding; its engagement included 35 provider meetings (~596 attendees) and 57 hospital leadership/board meetings.
source_quote: Hospital Leadership and Boards 57 243 ... Provider Meetings 35 596

quote: before Act 68 global budgets take effect (FY2028)
correct_fact: Act 68: one or more non-CAH hospitals from FY2028 and all hospitals by FY2030, both to the extent resources are available.
source_quote: Beginning not later than HFY2028, to the extent that resources are available ... one or more Vermont hospitals that are not critical access hospitals

quote: $5.8M reduced expenditure per $1M PCMH investment
correct_fact: Jones 2016: per $1M spent on the Blueprint initiative (PCMH + CHT + program), 2008-2013 data.
source_quote: medical expenditures decreased by approximately $5.8 million for every $1 million spent on the Blueprint initiative

quote: Vermont MHI pilot: PHQ-9 improvement
correct_fact: MHI quantitative/claims evaluations results 'anticipated in early 2026'; first-year data show screening increases, not PHQ-9 outcome improvement.
source_quote: A quantitative evaluation ... and a difference-in-difference study of Medicaid claims data are also underway ... Results are anticipated in early 2026

quote: Vermont: 6 certified CCBHCs (4 added July 1, 2026); enhanced Medicaid FMAP for the 4-year demonstration
correct_fact: Matches VERIFIED_FACTS (see WCMHS caveat in ch08 finding).
source_quote: CCBHC: 4 certified July 1, 2026 ... + Clara Martin and Rutland MH earlier = 6.

quote: CKD staging, DM complications, morbid obesity --- most common VT gaps
correct_fact: Superlative unsourced.

quote: Work This Chapter: Clinical Quality Optimizer /research-lab/policy-quality?tab=quality; High vs. Low Value Care ?tab=value; Risk Stratification Engine ?tab=risk; Academy lesson 'Quality Mechanics --- HEDIS, HCC, and Measuring What Matters'; /academy/tracks/clinical-quality-measurement
correct_fact: All tools tagged ch 9 in tools.ts; tabs render; Optimizer has HEDIS, Star and MIPS/APM tabs with bonus estimates; High/Low Value has Choosing Wisely scan and VBC savings; Risk engine has care-management coverage gap section. Lesson published with sanity_slug; Clinical Quality Measurement course published with tracks HEDIS and CAHPS / CMS Quality Programs / eCQMs and FHIR.
source_quote: // Care-management coverage gap — Chapter 9's 'gap quality measures do not surface'

quote: The HSA Coordinator model --- placing dedicated transformation coordinators in each HSA ... the AHS restructuring Vermont's transformation requires
correct_fact: HSA Coordinators are this book's proposal (Ch11 §11.x 'this book proposes'; Ch16), not an AHS model; the Act 119 report (Feb 2026) recommended keeping AHS unified rather than restructuring.
source_quote: Act 119 of 2024 ... Feb 4, 2026 report: keep AHS unified

quote: The CCBHC expansion Vermont is pursuing through the RHT Program creates a network ... across all HSAs
correct_fact: CCBHC expansion runs through the federal CCBHC (Section 223) demonstration with enhanced Medicaid; RHT has no CCBHC funding line. Six CCBHCs cover ~80% of the state, not all HSAs yet.
source_quote: Vermont became an official CCBHC Demonstration State in 2024

quote: Coleman EA, et al. Transitional Care Model documentation
correct_fact: The Transitional Care Model is Mary Naylor's (Penn); Eric Coleman developed the separate Care Transitions Intervention.
source_quote: The Transitional Care Model (TCM) ... developed by Mary Naylor
